newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke rounds on dissident Conservatives.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke rounds on dissident Conservatives.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Thursday rounded on dissident Conservative MPs, accusing them of making the party impossible for Prime Minister John Major to lead.
"John can lead a party, but there are sometimes parties that are simply not capable of being led," Clarke said in response to a question in a BBC radio programme.
Clarke said the Conservatives ought to be poised for another general election victory given the buoyant state of the economy.
"John Major should be on to a walk-over at the next election. I cannot believe that we have got ourselves behind in the polls," he said.
The problem, he said, lay "with some of those people on the backbenches in the Conservative Party in Parliament."

Clarke had been asked to comment on an anonymous article by a backbench MP in the left wing weekly Tribune, which described Major as "terminally inadequate at defending Britain's interests and leading our party".

"If the backbenches of the Conservative Party would only come to their senses and stop writing rubbish like that in Tribune, we could beat this inadequate Labour Party completely out of sight," he said.
